key_insight: Domain-specific biomedical text embeddings, especially BioBERT, helped identify clinical-trial dosing errors better than general or stacked embeddings.
clinical_relevance: This could support earlier trial safety screening by flagging protocols at higher risk of dosing mistakes, helping protect participants and improve oversight.
method: Encoded clinical-trial text with ClinicalBERT, PubMedBERT, BioBERT, and MedCPT.
Compared classical ML and neural models for dosing-error prediction.
evidence_signal: Using ROC-AUC, BioBERT reached 0.794 with logistic regression, and the strongest models overall achieved 0.821 to 0.853.
watch_item: Results are promising but should be validated on external datasets before being used in real-world regulatory or trial-monitoring workflows.
paper_title: CaresAI at CT-DEB26: Detecting Dosing Errors In Clinical Trials Using Domain-Specific Transformer Embeddings and Classification Models
